title: DreamShaper replaces Sana Sprint
summary:
DreamShaper replaced Sana Sprint, community models gained fallback routes, and image-input errors became easier to handle.

DreamShaper 8 LCM replaced Sana Sprint in the image model listing, with `sana` retained as an alias for existing callers. The worker uses a fixed three-step configuration. A separate worker update added a concurrency setting; testing measured about 8 images per second per card with three processes, up from about 4.3 with one.

Community model owners can set up to three ordered fallback models in the model dialog or Polli CLI. Text and image requests can try eligible backups after upstream or network failures, but not after caller errors or content-policy refusals. Callers pay only for the model that completes the request, at no more than the requested model’s price.

Image generation, vision, 3D and embeddings now share image-download handling, including a 20MB per-image limit. Invalid URLs, failed downloads, oversized images and unsupported media return HTTP 400 with stable error codes instead of passing through an image host’s response status.
